free_tier.stated: USD 2.00/month for Nitro 1 on a 1 Gbps port, printed on the vendor's own LEB page against a struck-through USD 4.00: 1 vCPU on an AMD EPYC 75F3, 2 GB RAM, 30 GB NVMe. The Nitro ladder continues: Nitro 2 USD 4.00 (2 vCPU, 4 GB, 50 GB), Nitro 3 USD 8.00 (4 vCPU, 8 GB, 100 GB), Nitro 4 USD 16.00 (8 vCPU, 16 GB, 200 GB), Nitro 5 USD 32.00 (12 vCPU, 32 GB, 400 GB); the Ryzen 9 9950X3D line is USD 2.50/month for Ultra 1 (1 vCPU, 2 GB, 30 GB), USD 5.00 for Ultra 2, USD 10.00 for Ultra 3, USD 20.00 for Ultra 4 and USD 40.00 for Ultra 5 (same shapes). The page prints monthly prices only and no annual or renewal price; the offer post's annual figures are third-party and not carried here. The Deploy buttons do not open the VirtFusion panel: each plan's button carries its own cart link at godlike.host/cart-vps with productId, billingCycle=monthly, the LEB50 promo and a 50 discount; the cart page renders for an anonymous visitor and loads its prices with a script call this toolchain cannot make (a POST to the site's own preinstall API; the WHMCS order form for the plan answers 200 with no price in its static HTML), so the cart's own prices are unverified: behind a script. No sold-out marker and no coming-soon flag on any of the ten plan cards.

egress.terms: 5 TB of outbound transfer a month, stated on the LEB page beside 'Unmetered Inbound Traffic'; no overage price is printed

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: the vendor page names a VirtFusion control panel and one-click backups; no API, rclone backend or CLI is documented on the page read
chaining: USD 2.00/month for 2 GB and 30 GB on an EPYC 75F3 with a 1 Gbps port is one of the lowest 2 GB rates among evaluated providers, and Los Angeles plus New Jersey plus Amsterdam on one account makes it a candidate for a small always-on worker near the bytes it fetches; the missing traffic figure is the reason to test before committing a crawler to it.

limits.value: no monthly byte allowance appears on either page read, so nothing volume-shaped is binding: the 1 Gbps port is the only stated limit and throughput is therefore the wall. That is an inference from the plan card, which prints 'Network 1 Gbps' and no traffic figure, and not a vendor statement about shaping.

notes: verification criteria: whether the USD 2.00/month card price renews at USD 2.00 or reverts to the struck USD 4.00, and whether any monthly transfer allowance exists at all. The two pages disagree on the annual arithmetic: USD 1.83 x 12 is not USD 21.99 and USD 2.00 x 12 is USD 24.00, so the card and the post are pricing different billing terms and only the post says which.
